page: Microsoft Azure M64ls is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8280M processors running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with two threads per core, alongside 38 MB of shared L3 cache and support for AVX-512 vector instructions. Memory provisioning stands at 512 GB of RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Local storage consists of a bundled 2199 GB SSD, and the instance includes zero integrated hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate specialized capabilities characterized by high memory throughput alongside moderate multi-threaded compute density. In memory subsystem testing, the instance achieved 210.73 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations, placing it in the top 25% of tested systems. Cached memory reads and write bandwidth perform within the median range at 2439.97 GB/sec and 90.27 GB/sec respectively. Synthetic CPU evaluations reflect moderate aggregate throughput, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 9711.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 35347.1. Single-threaded performance exhibits a pronounced bottleneck, recording bottom-decile scores across single-core stress-ng tests, gzip compression (17.27 GB/sec), and text processing benchmarks.

The hardware configuration trades single-thread execution efficiency for substantial memory capacity, robust uncached memory bandwidth, and integrated high-capacity local scratch disk space. Applications relying on heavy single-thread sequential processing or intensive LLM token generation encounter performance restrictions on this platform. Conversely, the dense memory allocation and balanced parallel compute profile deliver steady throughput for memory-resident enterprise workloads, making the M64ls suited for in-memory databases, large Redis caches, intermediate data processing, and enterprise application backends requiring up to 512 GB of RAM.
